+# .claude/data/floor.yaml — the one tracked floor source (cycle-129 SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166).
+#
+# The floor is the set of guards, config keys and files no profile, knob or
+# cycle task may weaken. Readers:
+#   - .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh and tests/unit/guard-origins.bats: the
+#     `floor: true` rows of .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml equal floor_guards.
+#   - tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats: every floor_files entry (and the corpus
+#     rows named under floor_corpus) is byte-identical to origin/main.
+#   - tests/unit/profile-floor.bats (Sprint 2): profiles.yaml names no floor_keys.
+# Both bats suites pin this file's sha256; an edit fails until the pin is
+# deliberately updated in the same change (see the FLOOR_SHA256 constant).
+schema_version: 1
+
+floor_guards:
+  - fence:FR-1.2b
+  - fence:FR-SZ
+  - fence:FR-SZ-COPY
+  - fence:FR-SZ-DD
+  - fence:FR-SZ-EXTRACT
+  - fence:FR-SZ-INPLACE
+  - fence:FR-SZ-INTERP
+  - fence:FR-SZ-LINK
+  - fence:FR-SZ-REDIR
+  - fence:FR-SZ-TEE
+  - fence:FR-SZ2
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-COPY
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-INPLACE
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-REDIR
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-RM
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-TEE
+  - gate:verdict-derive
+  - gate:adversarial-review-gate
+  - policy:permission-deny-list
+  - policy:verdict-one-way-rule
+  - policy:operator-only-commands
+
+floor_keys:
+  - flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled
+  - flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled
+  - "flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice"
+  - "destructive_command_guard.*"
+  - "implement_gate.*"
+  - hounfour.locality
+
+# Paths whose bytes must not change relative to origin/main during a cycle.
+floor_files:
+  - .claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh
+  - .claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh
+  - .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json
+  - .claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt
+
+# Fence-corpus rows (by their `rule` field) that must not change relative to
+# origin/main. A trailing `*` is a prefix match.
+floor_corpus:
+  file: tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl
+  rules:
+    - FR-1.2b
+    - "FR-SZ*"

@@ -0,0 +1,905 @@
+# .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml — the guard origin map (cycle-129 SDD D-1.1, §3.1).
+#
+# The one hand-written input of the guard register. `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh`
+# enumerates the guards from the repository (hook commands in .claude/settings.json,
+# `# @guard fence:<id>` markers in block-destructive-bash.sh, `# @guard validator:<id>`
+# markers in validate-artifact.sh) and fails (exit 5) when one has no row here, when a
+# row here resolves to nothing, or when a row's origin is empty. It then writes the
+# tracked structural register grimoires/loa/guards.md and the untracked host yield
+# .run/guard-yield.{md,json}. Regenerate after editing: .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table
+#
+# Row fields:
+#   id             hook:<path under .claude/hooks> (scripts outside it: hook:scripts/<name>),
+#                  fence:<pattern id>, validator:<type>.<rule>, gate:<name>, policy:<name>;
+#                  ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$
+#   kind           hook | fence | validator | gate | policy
+#   class          harness (the model cannot override it) | script (a script checks or
+#                  reports) | prose (the model is asked to comply)
+#   status         active | dormant (armed only by the env var named in knob) |
+#                  telemetry (observes and logs, never refuses)
+#   origin         {kind: kf|issue|finding|cycle|design, ref: <non-empty>}; design rows
+#                  cite the commit that added the guard (git log --follow --diff-filter=A)
+#   knob           the config key or env var that arms, relaxes or disables it, or none
+#   floor          true exactly for the ids in .claude/data/floor.yaml floor_guards
+#   registrations  hook rows: every "<Event>:<matcher>" (or "<Event>" when the
+#                  registration has no matcher) from .claude/settings.json; [] otherwise
+#   script         gate and policy rows: the file that implements it (must exist)
+#   note           one line; the hooks-reference table's Purpose column for hook rows
+schema_version: 1
+guards:
+  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- hooks
+  - id: hook:scripts/upgrade-health-check.sh
+    kind: hook
+    class: script
+    status: active
+    origin: {kind: design, ref: "v1.5.0 692aa617"}
+    knob: none
+    floor: false
+    registrations: ["Setup"]
+    note: "Post-install and post-upgrade health check of the framework mount"
+  - id: hook:scripts/check-updates.sh
+    kind: hook
+    class: script
+    status: active
+    origin: {kind: design, ref: "v0.14.0 1f448140"}
+    knob: update_check.enabled
+    floor: false
+    registrations: ["SessionStart"]
+    note: "Notify when a newer framework release exists (cached; LOA_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=1 silences it)"
+  - id: hook:session-start/loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh
+    kind: hook
+    class: script
+    status: active
+    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-098 FR-L6 (#771)"}
+    knob: structured_handoff.enabled
+    floor: false
+    registrations: ["SessionStart"]
+    note: "Surface unread L6 structured handoffs inside a data fence"
+  - id: hook:session-start/loa-l7-surface-soul.sh
+    kind: hook
+    class: script
+    status: active
+    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-098 FR-L7"}
+    knob: soul_identity_doc.enabled
+    floor: false
+    registrations: ["SessionStart"]
+    note: "Surface the L7 soul identity document inside a data fence"
+  - id: hook:session-start/loa-run-mode-session-title.sh
+    kind: hook
+    class: script
+    status: active

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: plugin-authoring
commands.description: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.

commands.name: implement
commands.description: Execute sprint tasks with production-quality code and tests (from pr/head/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under pr/head/) (project)

commands.name: review-sprint
commands.description: Validate sprint implementation against acceptance criteria (from pr/head/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under pr/head/) (project)

commands.name: agents
commands.description: (removed) Ask Claude to create/manage subagents, or edit .claude/agents/

commands.description: Teach auto mode about your environment, plus optional rule tweaks

commands.description: Start a new session with empty context; previous session stays on disk (resumable with /resume)

commands.description: Set the prompt bar color for this session

#!/usr/bin/env bash # ============================================================================= # guard-yield.sh — the guard register and its 30-day host yield (cycle-129 FR-1) # ============================================================================= # Enumerates every guard Loa ships and joins it with its origin and its yield: # hooks every command registered in .claude/settings.json, parsed against # the canonical schema "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"/.claude/ [args] # (or the same wrapped in hook-guard.sh); one row per unique script # fences the `# @guard fence:` markers in block-destructive-bash.sh, # cross-checked both ways against its emit_block call sites and # its literal `pattern_id: ""` audit constants # validators the `# @guard validator:` markers in validate-artifact.sh # gates the fixed list in the origin map (each row's `script` must exist) # policies the floor policies in the origin map # Origins, class, status, knob and floor come from .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml; # the floor set must equal .claude/data/floor.yaml floor_guards. # # Outputs: # grimoires/loa/guards.md tracked, STRUCTURAL ONLY (a pure function of the # repository; no timestamp, no yield) — --check gates it # .run/guard-yield.md, .json untracked host yield: blocks_30d, likely_fp_30d, # telemetry_30d, last_real_catch per guard # hooks-reference.md table with --hooks-table, the rows between # and # # Yield (SDD D-1.3): rows of .run/audit.jsonl and its rotated segments # .run/audit.jsonl.* with action == "block", plus implement-gate rows (telemetry # when action is telemetry or ask), with ts inside the window. Replays are # excluded and counted: replay == true (LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 at the source), or, # for rows that predate the flag, a cwd under ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ or containing # /bats-run-, /bats., /evals/results/ or /sandbox/, or a UTC minute holding # BURST_ROWS (10) or more block rows (a suite replaying fixtures into the live # log from inside the repository; no interactive session blocks ten commands in # one minute). A block is a likely false # positive (a heuristic) when its command holds a heredoc (`<<`; or, when # .claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh defines heredoc_nonexec, a heredoc # that function calls non-executing), when its cwd lies outside the repository # (this checkout and its main worktree), or when its pattern id is a prose class # (SP-1, FR-MERGE-2, FR-2-AMBIGUOUS) with no destructive verb at statement start. # A real catch is a block that is not a likely false positive. # # Privacy: no command text, cwd, hostname, user or model name is written to any # output; ids match ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$; origin text comes from the tracked map. # # Usage: # guard-yield.sh [--window-days 30] [--audit-log PATH] [--origins PATH] # [--floor PATH] [--out grimoires/loa/guards.md] [--yield-dir .run] # [--hooks-table] [--check] [--json] [--root DIR] # [--settings PATH] [--fence PATH] [--validator PATH] # [--hooks-ref PATH] [--now YYYY-MM-DD|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ|EPOCH] # # Exit codes: # 0 written, or in sync (--check) # 1 drift (--check): guards.md or the hooks table differ from what would be written # 2 usage error # 3 unreadable or unparseable input (a missing audit log is a WARN and an empty yield) # 5 a guard without an origin row, a row that resolves to nothing, an invalid row, # a floor mismatch, or a hook command outside the canonical schema # # Tested by tests/unit/guard-yield.bats and tests/unit/guard-origins.bats. # ============================================================================= set -euo pipefail export LC_ALL=C SCRIPT_NAME="guard-yield.sh" SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)" usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Tested/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//' -e '/^Tested/d' } die() { local code="$1"; shift; echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: $*" >&2; exit "$code"; } warn() { echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: WARN: $*" >&2; } ROOT="" WINDOW_DAYS=30 AUDIT_LOG="" ORIGINS="" FLOOR="" OUT="" YIELD_DIR="" HOOKS_REF="" SETTINGS="" FENCE="" VALIDATOR="" NOW="" DO_HOOKS_TABLE=0 DO_CHECK=0 DO_JSON=0 need_arg() { [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die 2 "$1 needs a value (see --help)"; } while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do case "$1" in --window-days) need_arg "$@"; WINDOW_DAYS="$2"; shift 2 ;; --audit-log) need_arg "$@"; AUDIT_LOG="$2"; shift 2 ;; --origins) need_arg "$@"; ORIGINS="$2"; shift 2 ;; --floor) need_arg "$@"; FLOOR="$2"; shift 2 ;; --out) need_arg "$@"; OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;; --yield-dir) need_arg "$@"; YIELD_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;; --root) need_arg "$@"; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;; --settings) need_arg "$@"; SETTINGS="$2"; shift 2 ;; --fence) need_arg "$@"; FENCE="$2"; shift 2 ;; --validator) need_arg "$@"; VALIDATOR="$2"; shift 2 ;; --hooks-ref) need_arg "$@"; HOOKS_REF="$2"; shift 2 ;; --now) need_arg "$@"; NOW="$2"; shift 2 ;; --hooks-table) DO_HOOKS_TABLE=1; shift ;; --check) DO_CHECK=1; shift ;; --json) DO_JSON=1; shift ;; -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;; *) die 2 "unknown argument '$1' (see --help)" ;; esac done [[ "$WINDOW_DAYS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$WINDOW_DAYS" -ge 1 && "$WINDOW_DAYS" -le 3650 ]] \ || die 2 "--window-days must be an integer from 1 to 3650 (got '$WINDOW_DAYS')" command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 3 "jq is required" command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 3 "yq v4 (mikefarah) is required" case "$(yq --version 2>&1 || true)" in *mikefarah*"version v4."*) ;; *) die 3 "yq v4 (mikefarah) is required; found: $(yq --version 2>&1 | head -1)" ;; esac if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/../.."; fi [[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die 3 "--root '$ROOT' is not a directory" ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)" : "${ORIGINS:=$ROOT/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml}" : "${FLOOR:=$ROOT/.claude/data/floor.yaml}" : "${OUT:=$ROOT/grimoires/loa/guards.md}" : "${YIELD_DIR:=$ROOT/.run}" : "${SETTINGS:=$ROOT/.claude/settings.json}" : "${FENCE:=$ROOT/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh}" : "${VALIDATOR:=$ROOT/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh}" : "${HOOKS_REF:=$ROOT/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md}" : "${AUDIT_LOG:=$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl}" HEREDOC_LIB="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh" BURST_ROWS=10 REGEN_HINT="regenerate: .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table" # The time base: --now, else the clock. Day granularity is all any output shows. if [[ -z "$NOW" ]]; then NOW_EPOCH="$(date -u +%s)" elif [[ "$NOW" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then NOW_EPOCH="$NOW" elif [[ "$NOW" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$ ]]; then NOW_EPOCH="$(jq -rn --arg d "${NOW}T00:00:00Z" '$d | fromdateiso8601')" || die 2 "--now '$NOW' is not a date" elif [[ "$NOW" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$ ]]; then NOW_EPOCH="$(jq -rn --arg d "$NOW" '$d | fromdateiso8601')" || die 2 "--now '$NOW' is not a timestamp" else die 2 "--now takes YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or epoch seconds (got '$NOW')" fi TMPWORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/guard-yield.XXXXXX")" cleanup() { rm -rf -- "$TMPWORK"; } trap cleanup EXIT # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- inputs for f in "$ORIGINS" "$FLOOR" "$SETTINGS" "$FENCE" "$VALIDATOR"; do [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || die 3 "input not readable: $f" done MAP_JSON="$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ORIGINS" 2>/dev/null)" || die 3 "origin map does not parse as YAML: $ORIGINS" [[ -n "$MAP_JSON" && "$MAP_JSON" != "null" ]] || die 3 "origin map is empty: $ORIGINS" FLOOR_JSON="$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$FLOOR" 2>/dev/null)" || die 3 "floor file does not parse as YAML: $FLOOR" jq -e 'type == "object"' "$SETTINGS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 3 "settings file does not parse as a JSON object: $SETTINGS" ERRORS="$TMPWORK/errors" : > "$ERRORS" # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- map schema jq -r ' def idok: type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$"); def nonempty: type == "string" and length > 0; (if .schema_version != 1 then "origin map: schema_version must be 1" else empty end), (if (.guards | type) != "array" then "origin map: guards must be a list" else ((.guards | map(.id) | group_by(.) | map(select(length > 1) | .[0]))[] | "origin map: duplicate id \(tostring)"), (.guards[] | . as $r | ($r.id | tostring) as $id | (if ($r.id | idok | not) then "origin map: row id \($id) does not match ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$" else empty end), (if (($r.kind // "") | IN("hook","fence","validator","gate","policy") | not) then "\($id): kind must be hook|fence|validator|gate|policy" else empty end), (if ($id | startswith(($r.kind // "?") + ":") | not) then "\($id): the id prefix must equal its kind" else empty end), (if (($r.class // "") | IN("harness","script","prose") | not) then "\($id): class must be harness|script|prose" else empty end), (if (($r.status // "") | IN("active","dormant","telemetry") | not) then "\($id): status must be active|dormant|telemetry" else empty end), (if ($r.origin.ref | nonempty | not) then "guard \($id) has no origin (origin.ref is empty)" else empty end), (if (($r.origin.kind // "") | IN("kf","issue","finding","cycle","design") | not) then "\($id): origin.kind must be kf|issue|finding|cycle|design" else empty end), (if ($r.knob | nonempty | not) then "\($id): knob must be a config key, an env var or none" else empty end), (if ($r.floor | type) != "boolean" then "\($id): floor must be true or false" else empty end), (if (($r.registrations // []) | type != "array" or any(.[]; type != "string")) then "\($id): registrations must be a list of strings" else empty end), (if $r.status == "dormant" and (($r.knob // "") | test("^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$") | not) then "\($id): a dormant row names the arming env var in knob" else empty end), (if ($r.kind == "gate" or $r.kind == "policy") and ($r.script | nonempty | not) then "\($id): gate and policy rows name their script" else empty end), (if ($r.note // "" | type) != "string" then "\($id): note must be a string" else empty end) ) end) ' <<<"$MAP_JSON" >> "$ERRORS" || die 3 "origin map could not be checked: $ORIGINS" if [[ -s "$ERRORS" ]]; then sed "s/^/$SCRIPT_NAME: /" "$ERRORS" >&2 exit 5 fi # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- hooks # jq parses each registered command against the canonical schema; bash resolves # symlinks once and checks the script exists. US (0x1f) separates fields so an # empty matcher survives `read`. US=$'\x1f' HOOK_LINES="$TMPWORK/hooks.lines" jq -r ' def pfx: "\"\\$\\(git rev-parse --show-toplevel\\)\"/\\.claude/"; def path_re: "(?

[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+)"; def args_re: "(?( [A-Za-z0-9._=-]+)*)"; def badpath: split("/") | any(.[]; . == "" or . == "." or . == ".."); (.hooks // {}) | to_entries[] | .key as $e | (.value // [])[] | (.matcher // "") as $m | (.hooks // [])[] | (.command // "") as $c | ( ([$c | capture("^" + pfx + "hooks/hook-guard\\.sh " + pfx + path_re + args_re + "$")?] | .[0]) as $w | if $w != null then (if ($w.p | badpath) then ["bad", $c] else ["ok", $e, $m, $w.p, "1"] end) else (([$c | capture("^" + pfx + path_re + args_re + "$")?] | .[0]) as $d | if $d != null and ($d.p != "hooks/hook-guard.sh") and ($d.p | badpath | not) then ["ok", $e, $m, $d.p, "0"] else ["bad", $c] end) end ) | if any(.[]; explode | any(.[]; . < 32 or . == 127)) then ["bad", "(a command with control characters)"] else . end | join("\u001f") ' "$SETTINGS" > "$HOOK_LINES" || die 3 "settings hooks could not be enumerated: $SETTINGS" HOOK_ROWS="$TMPWORK/hooks.jsonl" : > "$HOOK_ROWS" while IFS="$US" read -r tag ev mt rel wrapped; do [[ -n "$tag" ]] || continue if [[ "$tag" != "ok" ]]; then echo "hook command outside the canonical schema \"\$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)\"/.claude/ [args] (or wrapped in hook-guard.sh): $ev" >> "$ERRORS" continue fi abs="$ROOT/.claude/$rel" if [[ -L "$abs" ]]; then tgt="$(readlink "$abs")" case "$tgt" in /*) ;; *) tgt="$(dirname "$abs")/$tgt" ;; esac tdir="$(cd "$(dirname "$tgt")" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || tdir="" canon="$tdir/$(basename "$tgt")" case "$canon" in "$ROOT/.claude/"*) rel="${canon#"$ROOT/.claude/"}"; abs="$canon" ;; *) echo "hook script .claude/$rel is a symlink that leaves .claude/ (registered for $ev)" >> "$ERRORS"; continue ;; esac fi if [[ ! -f "$abs" ]]; then echo "hook script .claude/$rel registered for $ev does not exist" >> "$ERRORS" continue fi case "$rel" in hooks/*) id="hook:${rel#hooks/}" ;; *) id="hook:$rel" ;; esac if [[ -n "$mt" ]]; then reg="$ev:$mt"; else reg="$ev"; fi jq -cn --arg id "$id" --arg rel "$rel" --arg ev "$ev" --arg mt "$mt" --arg reg "$reg" --arg w "$wrapped" \ '{id: $id, rel: $rel, event: $ev, matcher: $mt, registration: $reg, wrapped: ($w == "1")}' >> "$HOOK_ROWS" done < "$HOOK_LINES" HOOKS_JSON="$(jq -cs '.' "$HOOK_ROWS")" # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- fence markers # Sites: `emit_block ""` calls and literal `pattern_id: ""` audit constants on # non-comment lines. Each site needs a marker with its id within the 8 lines above; # each marker needs a site with its id within the 8 lines below. FENCE_IDS="$TMPWORK/fence.ids" awk -v errs="$ERRORS" ' function note(s) { print s >> errs } /^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*@guard[[:space:]]+fence:/ { s = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*@guard[[:space:]]+fence:/, "", s); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", s) if (s !~ /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/) { note("fence marker at line " NR " has an invalid id"); next } nm++; mline[nm] = NR; mid[nm] = s; next } /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next } { line = $0 if (line ~ /emit_block[[:space:]]*\(\)/) next while (match(line, /emit_block[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+/)) { tok = substr(line, RSTART, RLENGTH); line = substr(line, RSTART + RLENGTH) sub(/^emit_block[[:space:]]+/, "", tok) if (tok ~ /^"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"$/) { gsub(/"/, "", tok); ns++; sline[ns] = NR; sid[ns] = tok } else note("fence emit_block call at line " NR " has a non-literal pattern id; give it a literal id and a # @@ -50,11 +50,15 @@ ## Language
 **Jack in**: To start an autonomous run under run mode; a run that has finished or been stopped for good has jacked out.
 _Aliases_: jack out
 
+**Judgment**: The task kind for work that needs reading and a decision; it ships as prose or a reviewed artifact, and its sprint task line ends with kind: judgment.
+
 **Kaironic**: Stopping at the right moment rather than after a fixed count: an iterative review loop ends when successive passes stop finding material issues.
 _Avoid_: converged
 
 **Karpathy principles**: The four working rules applied on every code-touching turn: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes and goal-driven verification.
 
+**Kind counts**: The release-notes line that counts a cycle's sprint tasks by kind (mechanical, judgment and operator), read from the tagged task lines of its sprint plan.
+
 **Known failure**: A recorded degradation with its symptom, the attempts made and a reading guide, consulted before triage so that prior dead ends are not retried.
 _Aliases_: KF
 
@@ -62,6 +66,10 @@ ## Language
 
 **Map epic**: The epic bead that parents an effort's decision tickets, paired with a map document of its destination, decisions so far, fog and exclusions; run mode never implements it.
 
+**Mechanical**: The task kind for work a script could do reliably; it ships as code with tests, and a review flags a mechanical task delivered as prose the model re-executes.
+
+**Operator**: The human who owns the project and its decisions; as a task kind, work that belongs to that human, which a review flags when it was completed unattended without a decision:unblock ticket or a DEC row.
+
 **Round**: One frontier of interview questions asked together and answered together.
 
 **Run mode**: Unattended execution of a sprint plan with a circuit breaker, wrapping implement, review and audit in a loop. Its states are running, halted and jacked out.
@@ -78,4 +86,6 @@ ## Language
 
 **Voice**: The party a decision or finding is attributed to: the operator, the agent, Flatline or dissent.
 
+**Volume ratio**: The release-notes line that sets a cycle's script lines changed against its prose bytes changed and its model calls; the model-call count is local to the host that ran the cycle.
+
 **Zone**: One of the three permission regions of a repository: the System zone holds the framework and is never edited by hand, the State zone is read and written freely, and the App zone needs confirmation before a write.

 # Git Stash Safety
 
 `git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry.  `compare.sh` refuses a baseline whose `prompt_tree_sha` equals the tree under comparison, whose
 `captured_at_commit` is not a descendant of the suite's `ab.floor_commit`, or whose `corpus_sha256`
 drifted (`evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats`). Tests: `evals/tests/{execute-agent,eval-recall-grader,implement-discipline-grader,recall-baseline-freshness}.bats`.
+
+## Control arms and the record corpus (cycle-129 FR-2)
+
+Each recall suite pre-registers control arms in `ab.arms` (review: `baseline`, `no_companion`
+(informational), `no_karpathy`, `no_rule_files`; audit: `baseline`, `no_audit_delta`) and the verdict rule
+in `ab.threshold`. `execute-agent.sh` applies an arm (`LOA_EVAL_ARM`) to the sandbox copy only, after
+materialisation and immediately before the executor starts, and fails the trial (exit 2) when a toggle
+cannot take effect; `executor.json` records `arm`, `arm_toggles`, `arm_evidence`, `source_commit`,
+`models_used` and `refusal_fallbacks`. The executor never inherits the calling Claude Code session's
+coupling, and its subagent model is pinned to `EVAL_MODEL`.
+
+The record fixtures `pr-11` … `pr-18` are the round-1 states of sprints 247–254, built by
+`harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh` from `review-prs/record-pairs.tsv` and the `record/cycle-12x-a2a`
+branches. A feedback finding becomes a label only when the fix commit touches the file it cites. Labels
+live in the hidden `review-prs/labels/pr-NN.tsv` (never in the sandbox-copied `pr-NN/`), every drop is
+explained in `labels/pr-NN.dropped.txt`, and hand curation is the data file `labels/curation.tsv`,
+re-applied on every seed. `fix` rows (the hunks the fix commit changed) feed the grader's refuted share
+only. A label file is approved with `seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve pr-NN --by "<who> <date>"`;
+`run-arms.sh` refuses unapproved fixtures unless `--allow-unapproved`.
+
+```bash
+# one suite, one batch, against a detached worktree pinned at the source commit
+./evals/harness/run-arms.sh --suite review-recall --arms baseline,no_companion,no_karpathy,no_rule_files \
+  --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,pr-03,pr-04,pr-05,pr-06,pr-07,pr-08 --trials 3 --source-commit 864069f2 --dry-run
+./evals/harness/report.sh --arms            # refuses until STATUS.json is complete; --partial for interim
+./evals/harness/compare.sh --ab --arm-a evals/results/arms/review-recall/<batch>/baseline \
+  --arm-b evals/results/arms/review-recall/<batch>/no_karpathy --metric recall
+```
+
+Tests: `evals/tests/{arm-toggles,run-arms,arms-report,seed-corpus}.bats`.

     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# run-arms.sh — cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm driver (SDD D-2.3, DEC-0164, DEC-0171)
     4	#
     5	# Runs the declared control arms of one recall suite on a frozen fixture batch
     6	# against a detached git worktree pinned at --source-commit (never the live
     7	# tree), interleaving trials across arms so provider drift spreads evenly.
     8	#
     9	# Usage:
    10	#   run-arms.sh --suite review-recall|audit-recall --arms a,b,c
    11	#               --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,… --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
    12	#               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
    13	#               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
    14	#               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
    15	#
    16	# Per trial (fixture × arm × trial), in this order:
    17	#   1. the fixture's SHA256SUMS entries (its files, hidden manifest and labels)
    18	#      are verified; a drift stops the batch (state failed, exit 3). The whole
    19	#      corpus is verified once at batch start (digest in MANIFEST.json); each
    20	#      row records the SHA256SUMS digest seen at its trial, so approving another
    21	#      fixture's labels mid-batch is visible and harmless
    22	#   2. evals/harness/sandbox.sh creates the sandbox from the frozen fixture
    23	#   3. execute-agent.sh runs the executor with EVAL_PROMPT_TREE = the pinned
    24	#      worktree, LOA_EVAL_ARM = the arm (toggles hit the sandbox copy only),
    25	#      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT, EVAL_MODEL
    26	#   4. grade.sh grades it; the row goes to <batch>/<arm>/results.jsonl with
    27	#      arm, trial, source_commit, model_id, seed (null: the CLI route takes
    28	#      none) and run_date; the artifacts go under <batch>/<arm>/artifacts/
    29	#   A trial whose executor fails for a transport reason (timeout, no result
    30	#   event, API error, rate or session limit) is retried once after
    31	#   --retry-wait seconds; a second failure records an error row and the arm
    32	#   ends `partial`. Other executor failures are recorded, not retried.
    33	#
    34	# Layout: <results-dir>/<suite>/<batch>/{MANIFEST.json,STATUS.json,run.log,
    35	#   <arm>/results.jsonl,<arm>/artifacts/…}; <results-dir>/<suite>/STATUS.json
    36	#   aggregates every batch of the suite (the Sprint 2 gate and report.sh
    37	#   --arms read it). STATUS.json: {state: running|complete|partial|failed,
    38	#   per_arm: {<arm>: {trials_done, trials_failed, trials_planned}},
    39	#   source_commit, model_id, started, finished}.
    40	#
    41	# Exit: 0 complete, 1 partial (some trial failed twice; results kept),
    42	#       2 usage / refused before starting, 3 failed (no trial completed, or
    43	#       the corpus drifted mid-run)
    44	#
    45	# Executor: Fable 5.1 (D33, DEC-0164); the default --model is the id the
    46	# local claude CLI accepted on the cycle-129 probe (claude-fable-5-1).
    47	# Tested by evals/tests/run-arms.bats (stubbed CLI; no model call).
    48	# =============================================================================
    49	set -euo pipefail
    50	export LC_ALL=C

    52	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    53	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

    63	CONCURRENCY=2 BATCH="" RESULTS_ROOT="$EVALS_DIR/results/arms" RETRY_WAIT=300

    65	
    66	usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed -n '2,46p' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }

    73	    --fixtures) FIXTURES_CSV="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    74	    --trials) TRIALS="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    75	    --source-commit) SOURCE_COMMIT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    76	    --model) MODEL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    77	    --concurrency) CONCURRENCY="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;

   285	aggregate_status() {

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# run-arms.sh — cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm driver (SDD D-2.3, DEC-0164, DEC-0171)
     4	#
     5	# Runs the declared control arms of one recall suite on a frozen fixture batch
     6	# against a detached git worktree pinned at --source-commit (never the live
     7	# tree), interleaving trials across arms so provider drift spreads evenly.
     8	#
     9	# Usage:
    10	#   run-arms.sh --suite review-recall|audit-recall --arms a,b,c
    11	#               --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,… --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
    12	#               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
    13	#               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
    14	#               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
    15	#
    16	# Per trial (fixture × arm × trial), in this order:
    17	#   1. the fixture's SHA256SUMS entries (its files, hidden manifest and labels)
    18	#      are verified; a drift stops the batch (state failed, exit 3). The whole
    19	#      corpus is verified once at batch start (digest in MANIFEST.json); each
    20	#      row records the SHA256SUMS digest seen at its trial, so approving another
    21	#      fixture's labels mid-batch is visible and harmless
    22	#   2. evals/harness/sandbox.sh creates the sandbox from the frozen fixture
    23	#   3. execute-agent.sh runs the executor with EVAL_PROMPT_TREE = the pinned
    24	#      worktree, LOA_EVAL_ARM = the arm (toggles hit the sandbox copy only),
    25	#      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT, EVAL_MODEL
    26	#   4. grade.sh grades it; the row goes to <batch>/<arm>/results.jsonl with
    27	#      arm, trial, source_commit, model_id, seed (null: the CLI route takes
    28	#      none) and run_date; the artifacts go under <batch>/<arm>/artifacts/
    29	#   A trial whose executor fails for a transport reason (timeout, no result
    30	#   event, API error, rate or session limit) is retried once after
    31	#   --retry-wait seconds; a second failure records an error row and the arm
    32	#   ends `partial`. Other executor failures are recorded, not retried.
    33	#
    34	# Layout: <results-dir>/<suite>/<batch>/{MANIFEST.json,STATUS.json,run.log,
    35	#   <arm>/results.jsonl,<arm>/artifacts/…}; <results-dir>/<suite>/STATUS.json
    36	#   aggregates every batch of the suite (the Sprint 2 gate and report.sh
    37	#   --arms read it). STATUS.json: {state: running|complete|partial|failed,
    38	#   per_arm: {<arm>: {trials_done, trials_failed, trials_planned}},
    39	#   source_commit, model_id, started, finished}.
    40	#
    41	# Exit: 0 complete, 1 partial (some trial failed twice; results kept),
    42	#       2 usage / refused before starting, 3 failed (no trial completed, or
    43	#       the corpus drifted mid-run)
    44	#
    45	# Executor: Fable 5.1 (D33, DEC-0164); the default --model is the id the
    46	# local claude CLI accepted on the cycle-129 probe (claude-fable-5-1).
    47	# Tested by evals/tests/run-arms.bats (stubbed CLI; no model call).
    48	# =============================================================================
    49	set -euo pipefail
    50	export LC_ALL=C
    51	
    52	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    53	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

   132	# verify_corpus [<fixture>] — every SHA256SUMS entry (or one fixture's entries
   133	# and its manifest) hashes as recorded. Prints the SHA256SUMS digest.
   134	verify_corpus() {
   135	  python3 -I - "$CORPUS_DIR" "${1:-}" <<'PY'
   136	import hashlib, os, sys
   137	corpus, only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   138	sums = os.path.join(corpus, "SHA256SUMS")
   139	raw = open(sums, "rb").read()
   140	bad = []
   141	for line in raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines():
   142	    if not line.strip():
   143	        continue
   144	    digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
   145	    if only and not (rel.startswith(only + "/") or rel == f"manifests/{only}.json" or rel == "corpus.tsv"
   146	                     or rel.startswith(f"labels/{only}.")):
   147	        continue
   148	    p = os.path.join(corpus, rel)
   149	    if not os.path.isfile(p) or hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != digest:
   150	        bad.append(rel)
   151	if bad:
   152	    print("corpus drift: " + ", ".join(bad[:10]), file=sys.stderr)
   153	    sys.exit(1)
   154	print(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())
   155	PY
   156	}

   382	     + (if $executor == null then {} else {executor: $executor} end)' > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row.tmp"
   383	  mv "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row.tmp" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"
   384	}
   385	
   386	keep_artifacts() {  # keep_artifacts <ws> <arm> <task_id> <trial> <suffix>
   387	  local ws="$1" dest="$BATCH_DIR/$2/artifacts/$3/trial-$4$5" f
   388	  mkdir -p "$dest"
   389	  for f in executor.json agent-output.json agent-stderr.log arm-removed.txt; do
   390	    [[ -f "$ws/.eval/$f" ]] && cp "$ws/.eval/$f" "$dest/$f"
   391	  done
   392	  for f in review.md audit.md; do [[ -f "$ws/$f" ]] && cp "$ws/$f" "$dest/$f"; done
   393	  # the raw transcript only on request (it embeds every tool result)
   394	  [[ "${EVAL_KEEP_EVENTS:-0}" == "1" && -f "$ws/.eval/events.jsonl" ]] && cp "$ws/.eval/events.jsonl" "$dest/events.jsonl"
   395	  return 0
   396	}
   397	
   398	# Parent-side: append a finished job's row and update the counters.
   399	collect() {  # collect <job-id> <arm>
   400	  local jid="$1" arm="$2" i
   401	  i="$(arm_index "$arm")"
   402	  if [[ -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.flag" ]]; then
   403	    log "corpus drift before $jid: $(cat "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.drift" 2>/dev/null)"
   404	    set_state failed; exit 3
   405	  fi
   406	  if [[ -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" ]]; then
   407	    mkdir -p "$BATCH_DIR/$arm"
   408	    cat "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" >> "$BATCH_DIR/$arm/results.jsonl"
   409	    if [[ "$(jq -r '.status' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row")" == "completed" ]]; then
   410	      DONE[$i]=$(( ${DONE[$i]} + 1 ))
   411	      log "done $jid ($(jq -r '"\(.arm) \(.fixture) t\(.trial) recall=\(([.graders[]? | select(.name=="recall-vs-defects.sh") | .details.recall][0]) // "n/a") \(.duration_ms/1000|floor)s"' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"))"
   412	    else
   413	      FAILED[$i]=$(( ${FAILED[$i]} + 1 ))
   414	      log "FAILED $jid ($(jq -c '.error' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"))"
   415	    fi
   416	    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid".*
   417	  else
   418	    FAILED[$i]=$(( ${FAILED[$i]} + 1 ))
   419	    log "FAILED $jid (no row written; see $JOBS_DIR/$jid.exec.log)"
   420	  fi
   421	  write_status
   422	}
   423	
   424	log "start suite=$SUITE batch=$BATCH source=$SRC12 model=$MODEL trials=${#PLAN[@]} concurrency=$CONCURRENCY worktree=$WORKTREE"
   425	write_status
   426	trap 'log "interrupted"; set_state failed; exit 3' INT TERM HUP
   427	
   428	PIDS=() PJOB=() PARM=()
   429	reap() {  # reap until fewer than $1 jobs run
   430	  local i
   431	  while [[ ${#PIDS[@]} -ge $1 ]]; do
   432	    for i in "${!PIDS[@]}"; do
   433	      if ! kill -0 "${PIDS[$i]}" 2>/dev/null; then
   434	        wait "${PIDS[$i]}" 2>/dev/null || true
   435	        collect "${PJOB[$i]}" "${PARM[$i]}"
   436	        unset 'PIDS[i]' 'PJOB[i]' 'PARM[i]'
   437	        PIDS=("${PIDS[@]+"${PIDS[@]}"}"); PJOB=("${PJOB[@]+"${PJOB[@]}"}"); PARM=("${PARM[@]+"${PARM[@]}"}")
   438	        break
   439	      fi
   440	    done
   441	    [[ ${#PIDS[@]} -ge $1 ]] && sleep 1
   442	  done
   443	  return 0
   444	}
   445	
   446	n=0
   447	for p in "${PLAN[@]}"; do
   448	  IFS='|' read -r a f t <<<"$p"
   449	  n=$((n + 1)); jid="$(printf 'j%04d' "$n")"

   451	  run_trial "$jid" "$a" "$f" "$t" &
   452	  PIDS+=("$!"); PJOB+=("$jid"); PARM+=("$a")
   453	done
   454	reap 1
   455	
   456	total_done=0 total_failed=0
   457	for i in "${!ARMS[@]}"; do total_done=$(( total_done + ${DONE[$i]} )); total_failed=$(( total_failed + ${FAILED[$i]} )); done
   458	if [[ $total_failed -eq 0 ]]; then
   459	  set_state complete; log "complete: $total_done trials"; exit 0
   460	elif [[ $total_done -eq 0 ]]; then
   461	  set_state failed; log "failed: no trial completed ($total_failed failed)"; exit 3
   462	else
   463	  set_state partial; log "partial: $total_done done, $total_failed failed"; exit 1
   464	fi

+  # surface only, after materialisation and immediately before the executor

+    coverage_required: full

local glob_expanded=false
      for task_file in $EVALS_DIR/$pattern; do
        if [[ -f "$task_file" ]]; then
          TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
          glob_expanded=true
        fi
      done

      # Restore globstar
      if [[ "$had_globstar" == "false" ]]; then
        shopt -u globstar 2>/dev/null || true
      fi

      # Fallback: if glob didn't match, try find in the directory
      if [[ "$glob_expanded" == "false" ]]; then
        # Extract directory portion from pattern
        local pattern_dir="${pattern%/*}"
        if [[ -d "$EVALS_DIR/$pattern_dir" ]]; then
          while IFS= read -r -d '' task_file; do
            TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
          done < <(find "$EVALS_DIR/$pattern_dir" \( -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' \) -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
        fi
      fi
    done

    # Apply exclude patterns
    local exclude_count
    exclude_count="$(yq -r '.tasks.exclude | length // 0' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")"
    if [[ "$exclude_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
      local filtered_tasks=()
      for task_file in "${TASK_FILES[@]}"; do
        local excluded=false
        for j in $(seq 0 $((exclude_count - 1))); do
          local exclude_pattern
          exclude_pattern="$(yq -r ".tasks.exclude[$j]" "$suite_file")"
          if [[ "$(basename "$task_file")" == $exclude_pattern ]]; then
            excluded=true
            break
          fi
        done
        [[ "$excluded" == "false" ]] && filtered_tasks+=("$task_file")

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# seed-corpus-from-record.sh — build a review-recall fixture from a shipped
     4	# sprint's round-1 state and its record-branch feedback (cycle-129 FR-2,
     5	# SDD D-2.2, DEC-0154)
     6	#
     7	# Usage:
     8	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh <global-sprint> <record-ref> [--out <corpus>/pr-NN]
     9	#                              [--base <rev>] [--head <rev>] [--fix <rev>]
    10	#                              [--feedback a.md,b.md] [--dry-run]
    11	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --build-manifest pr-NN   # labels → hidden manifest (after curation)
    12	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve pr-NN --by "<who> <YYYY-MM-DD>"
    13	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --freeze                 # regenerate SHA256SUMS
    14	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --check                  # verify SHA256SUMS
    15	#   common: [--repo <git dir>] [--corpus <evals/fixtures/review-prs>]
    16	#
    17	# Without --base/--head/--fix/--feedback/--out the sprint's row in
    18	# <corpus>/record-pairs.tsv supplies them.
    19	#
    20	# Writes (seed):
    21	#   <corpus>/pr-NN/{fixture.yaml, head.diff, PR.md, REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md,
    22	#                   AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md, base/…, head/…}     (copied into the sandbox)
    23	#   <corpus>/labels/pr-NN.tsv          HIDDEN (never copied into a sandbox): the labels,
    24	#                                      first line `# approved-by: pending`
    25	#   <corpus>/labels/pr-NN.dropped.txt  HIDDEN: every finding that did not become a label, and why
    26	#   <corpus>/manifests/pr-NN.json      HIDDEN: the graded manifest (`approved: false` until --approve)
    27	#   <corpus>/corpus.tsv                one `record` row per fixture (or a `#` gap comment)
    28	#   evals/tasks/{review,audit}-recall/{review,audit}-pr-NN.yaml
    29	#   <corpus>/SHA256SUMS                refreshed
    30	#
    31	# Scope: the fixture is the change base..head without the generated or state
    32	# files (grimoires/, CHANGELOG.md, .claude/checksums.json, REPO-MAP.md, lock
    33	# files, .beads/, .run/, evals/results/) and without binaries.
    34	#
    35	# Label rule: a feedback finding becomes a label only when the fix commit
    36	# touches the file it cites (`git diff --name-only head..fix`) and that file
    37	# is part of the fixture; label_source is review (engineer-feedback*,
    38	# reviewer*), audit (auditor-sprint-feedback*) or bridgebuilder
    39	# (bridgebuilder*, the "Fixed" table only). The anchor is a head-side line
    40	# the fix changed near the cited line or inside the cited symbol; a finding
    41	# that cites only a file is anchored on that file's fix hunks when there are
    42	# at most four, else dropped. `fix` rows cover every hunk fix_commit changed
    43	# in a fixture file (source fix/<sha>:<start>-<end>); the grader uses them
    44	# only for refuted share. Titles are control-stripped, capped at 160 chars,
    45	# and a title matching a secret pattern drops its finding; every written
    46	# file passes evals/graders/no-secrets.sh or the seed fails.
    47	#
    48	# Exit: 0 ok, 1 refused / spec error / secret found / check failed, 2 usage
    49	# Tested by evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats.
    50	# =============================================================================
    51	set -euo pipefail
    52	export LC_ALL=C
    53	
    54	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    55	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    56	
    57	exec python3 -I - "$REPO_ROOT" "$@" <<'PY'
    58	import argparse, csv, hashlib, io, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile
    59	
    60	HARNESS_ROOT = sys.argv[1]
    61	argv = sys.argv[2:]
    62	
    63	ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="seed-corpus-from-record.sh", add_help=True)

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# Path-scoped rule files (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-3.1, DEC-0129): stash-safety.md and
+# skill-invariants.md carry `paths:` frontmatter, the frontmatter parses, and every glob
+# matches at least one tracked file of the kind the rule is about (git pathspec glob
+# semantics: `**` spans directories, `*` stays inside one).
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    RULES="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/rules"
+    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not installed"
+}
+
+# The YAML between the first two '---' lines (empty when the file has none).
+frontmatter() { awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" { exit } /^---$/ { if (n++) exit; next } n' "$1"; }
+globs() { frontmatter "$1" | yq eval '.paths[]' -; }
+tracked() { git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" ls-files -- ":(glob)$1"; }
+
+@test "RP-1 both rule files open with frontmatter that parses and lists string globs under paths:" {
+    local f n
+    for f in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
+        [ "$(head -1 "$RULES/$f")" = "---" ] || { echo "$f has no frontmatter"; return 1; }
+        frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.' - >/dev/null || { echo "$f frontmatter does not parse"; return 1; }
+        [ "$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.paths | type' -)" = "!!seq" ]
+        n="$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.paths | length' -)"
+        [ "$n" -ge 1 ]
+        [ "$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '[.paths[] | select(type != "!!str")] | length' -)" -eq 0 ]
+    done
+}
+
+@test "RP-2 the globs are the ones the SDD names" {
+    [ "$(globs "$RULES/stash-safety.md" | tr '\n' ' ')" = '**/*.sh **/*.bats .claude/scripts/** .claude/hooks/** ' ]
+    [ "$(globs "$RULES/skill-invariants.md" | tr '\n' ' ')" = '.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md .claude/agents/** .claude/data/agent-types.yaml .claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh ' ]
+}
+

+    local g hits

+        [ -n "$hits" ] || { echo "glob '$g' matches no tracked .sh/.bats file"; return 1; }
+    done < <(globs "$RULES/stash-safety.md")

+        [ -n "$hits" ] || { echo "glob '$g' matches no tracked file of the intended kind"; return 1; }
+    done < <(globs "$RULES/skill-invariants.md")
+}
+
+@test "RP-5 path-scoping removed no rule text: the body after the frontmatter keeps its heading and sections" {
+    local body
+    body="$(awk '/^---$/ && c < 2 { c++; next } c >= 2' "$RULES/stash-safety.md")"
+    [[ "$body" == *"# Git Stash Safety"* && "$body" == *"## Judgment rules the fence cannot express"* ]]
+    body="$(awk '/^---$/ && c < 2 { c++; next } c >= 2' "$RULES/skill-invariants.md")"
+    [[ "$body" == *"# Skill Frontmatter Invariants"* && "$body" == *"## The invariant"* ]]

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the two release-notes lines of a cycle, task-kind
     4	# counts and the volume ratio (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).
     5	#
     6	#   kinds: mechanical N · judgment N · operator N
     7	#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>
     8	#
     9	# Mapping (the glossary's "Kind counts" and "Volume ratio" entries):
    10	#   kinds          the 'kind: <value>' token that ends each top-level '- [ ]' /
    11	#                  '- [x]' task line under '### Technical Tasks', and each
    12	#                  '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside
    13	#                  a '## Sprint N' block of the sprint plan (fenced code skipped,
    14	#                  the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces);
    15	#                  untagged task lines are counted in --json and WARNed
    16	#   script lines   added + deleted lines of *.sh *.py *.ts *.js files between
    17	#                  the two commits (git diff --numstat, renames detected,
    18	#                  binary files skipped)
    19	#   prose bytes    bytes of the added and removed *.md lines between the two
    20	#                  commits, newline included, diff markers excluded
    21	#   model calls    MODELINV rows (primitive_id MODELINV) in the MODELINV log

# --now: replay exclusion (flag, cwd, burst) counted in the header, the

# a destructive verb at statement start), day-granular last_real_catch, the

  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"

          model_id:"claude-fable-5-1", arms:["baseline","no_companion","no_karpathy","no_rule_files"], fixtures:["pr-01","pr-02","pr-03"], trials:3}' \
    > "$B/MANIFEST.json"
  status_file complete
}

teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

status_file() {  # status_file <state>
  jq -n --arg s "$1" '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", state:$s, batches:[{batch:"b1", state:$s}],
                       source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457", model_id:"claude-fable-5-1"}' > "$S/STATUS.json"
}

# row <arm> <fixture> <trial> <recall> <missed-csv> [<cited> <refuted> <model> <source>]

  local arm="$1" fx="$2" t="$3" rc="$4" missed="$5" cited="${6:-4}" ref="${7:-1}"
  local model="${8:-claude-fable-5-1}" src="${9:-864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457}"
  mkdir -p "$B/$arm"
  jq -cn --arg arm "$arm" --arg fx "$fx" --argjson t "$t" --argjson rc "$rc" --arg missed "$missed" \
    --argjson cited "$cited" --argjson ref "$ref" --arg model "$model" --arg src "$src" \
    '{status:"completed", arm:$arm, fixture:$fx, task_id:("review-" + $fx), trial:$t, model_id:$model, source_commit:$src,
      executor:{model_id:$model, usage:{input_tokens:100, cache_read_input_tokens:900, output_tokens:0, cache_creation_input_tokens:0}},
      graders:[{name:"recall-vs-defects.sh", details:{recall:$rc, planted:3,
        detected:[], missed:($missed | split(",") | map(select(length > 0))),
        findings_cited:$cited, findings_refuted:$ref}}]}' >> "$B/$arm/results.jsonl"
}

full_arm() {  # full_arm <arm> <recall> [<missed>] [<refuted>]
  local fx t
  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row "$1" "$fx" "$t" "$2" "${3:-}" 4 "${4:-1}"; done; done
}

head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:302 — [HIGH] The pre-registered verdict uses `abs(drop)`, so an arm whose mean recall IMPROVES on the baseline counts as a "named" drop. If that arm also breaks a recall rule (min-trial or CI upper bound), it reads **recall loss** instead of inconclusive. Reproduced: baseline mean 0.667 (spread 0); arm mean 0.778 with one weak trial → "recall loss", and line 324 prints "change named" for a drop of -0.111. This contradicts the docstring (lines 19-23: "the mean drop exceeds the baseline spread"). The test should be `drop > base_spread`, and line 324 needs the same fix.
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:266 — [MEDIUM] The `rule_files` toggle succeeds silently when neither stash-safety.md nor skill-invariants.md is in the sandbox. It records `removed: none present` and exits 0, so `no_rule_files` runs as the baseline, e.g. on a pinned source commit that predates the files or with no `.claude/rules/`. That breaks the contract in the header (lines 63-65: "a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never silently runs as its baseline)"). The other toggles fail closed, and AT-9 covers only karpathy_block and audit_delta_instruction. Fix: exit 2 when `gone` is empty.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:408 — [MEDIUM] Re-running a batch with the same source and model is allowed (line 254) but has no resume logic. The full PLAN runs again and every row is appended (`>>`) to `<arm>/results.jsonl` with the same trial numbers, while the batch STATUS counters restart from 0. arms-report.py reads every row: duplicated trials count toward trials_required, get averaged into the per-trial means, and fill coverage gaps that a partial run left. Fix: refuse a batch that already has results, skip trials that already completed, or truncate.
head/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md:3 — [MEDIUM] Path-scoping this rule to `**/*.sh`, `**/*.bats`, `.claude/scripts/**` and `.claude/hooks/**` ties it to editing shell files. The hazard it covers is a `git stash` Bash command run during any skill. Its own origin incident (line 41: Edit-tool NOTES.md updates lost, #555) touched no file in the scope, so the judgment rules the fence cannot express (`stash -k` with pre-commit, `fsck` before `gc`) stop loading in exactly that situation. The SDD reference does not explain why this is safe.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:655 — [MEDIUM] Hand curation matches a label only by its positional number prefix (`L03-`). Ids are assigned by parse order at line 644, so a re-seed that adds, removes or reorders a finding (a parser change, or another feedback file) silently applies a `drop` or `anchors` curation row to a different finding. The `len(hit) != 1` check cannot catch this. Fix: match the full id (number plus slug) or the source.
head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:518 — [LOW] Burst detection groups every block row in the window, including rows the cwd rule already classed as replays. Ten or more rows in one UTC minute then exclude every live row in that minute. A test suite replaying under /tmp therefore erases a real block that happens in the same minute, and so does an agent retrying a blocked command 10 times in a minute (the comment says this never happens, but it does in loops). Fix: compute bursts on rows not already excluded, and scope them by cwd.
head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:500 — [LOW] The replay heuristic matches the substrings `/sandbox/`, `/bats.` and `/evals/results/` anywhere in cwd. Every block from a real project under a path like ~/sandbox/app is excluded from the yield as a replay. Only replay_rows_by_rule.cwd shows this, and it does not name the cause.
head/evals/suites/review-recall.yaml:41 — [LOW] The `no_companion` arm cannot change the executor's behaviour. The executor is restricted to Read,Grep,Glob,Write (execute-agent.sh:320), so the companion voice (adversarial-review.sh, which needs Bash) never runs in either arm, and the arm will always report "no recall loss". The description also says only code_review.companion_voice is set, but execute-agent.sh sets security_audit too.
head/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:28 — [LOW] An out-of-scope, unexplained permission change: the implement skill's app-zone (src, lib, app) permission is widened from `read` to `read-write`. The PR description does not mention it, no test pins it, and it is unrelated to the guard register, control arms or task kinds. Split it out, or justify it in the PR.
head/.claude/data/floor.yaml:10 — [LOW] The comment says "Both bats suites pin this file's sha256". Only tests/unit/guard-origins.bats (FLOOR_SHA256) pins it, and floor-snapshot.bats skips entirely on a shallow checkout. Correct the comment so nobody assumes there is a second pin.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
The review is in `/workspace/review.md`, with 10 findings and the verdict **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. Nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**Blocking findings:**
- **`arms-report.py:302` (high, reproduced):** the verdict rule uses `abs(drop)`, so an arm that *improves* mean recall can be labelled **recall loss**. I ran it: baseline 0.667, arm 0.778 with one weak trial, and the report said "recall loss" and "change named". That contradicts the rule written in the script's own docstring.
- **`execute-agent.sh:266`:** the `rule_files` toggle exits 0 even when neither rule file exists. The `no_rule_files` arm then quietly runs as the baseline, which breaks the stated contract that a toggle that can't take effect fails with exit 2.
- **`run-arms.sh:408`:** re-running a batch with the same source and model is allowed, but there's no resume. Every trial runs again and is appended with the same trial numbers. The report then counts the duplicates as extra trials and as coverage.
- **`stash-safety.md:3`:** limiting the rule to shell-file paths means it doesn't load in the situation it came from: NOTES.md edits lost to `git stash` (issue #555).
- **`seed-corpus-from-record.sh:655`:** hand-curation rows match a label only by its position number (`L03-`). A re-seed that renumbers the labels silently applies the drop or re-anchor to a different finding.

**Lower-severity findings:** guard-yield's replay heuristics (burst and cwd-substring) can drop real blocks from the yield. The `no_companion` arm can't change anything, because the restricted executor has no Bash. There's an unexplained widening of the app-zone permission in implementing-tasks from read to read-write. And a comment in `floor.yaml` claims a second sha256 pin that doesn't exist.
